---
title: "Dry Run First"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** Ground Truth. **Objective:** check pipeline code an agent wrote cheaply, before it touches real data or a cluster queue.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">Last verified (docs, not run): Snakemake and Nextflow docs on 2026-11-13 (sources in `research/factory.md`). Not confirmed in the docs: exactly which wiring errors a Snakemake dry run reports, so treat that as typical behaviour, not a guarantee.</span>
:::

The Factory runs the same steps every time. When an agent writes or edits a pipeline, the danger is a rule that looks right and wires the wrong inputs, so that hours of compute are wasted or, worse, finish with a plausible wrong result.

Check in layers, cheapest first:

1. **Read the diff** (small, as in the Wall of Output).
2. **Dry run**: ask the workflow manager what it *would* run. It shows the plan (which files feed which steps). Nothing runs, so it cannot show the commands are correct.
3. **Stub run** (Nextflow) or a **tiny real input**: run the whole graph in seconds on a few records.
4. **Compare with ground truth** on that tiny input, as in Ground Truth.
5. Only then real data, through the scheduler if you are on a cluster.

::: {.panel-tabset group="engine"}

## Snakemake

`snakemake -n` (dry run) prints the jobs it would run and why, without running them. Use a small input file and compare the plan with what you expect.

## Nextflow

`nextflow run main.nf -stub-run` runs each process's `stub:` block instead of the real script, so the wiring is exercised quickly. `-resume` reuses cached results for tasks whose inputs and script are unchanged. A process **without** a `stub:` block runs its real script even under `-stub-run`, so check that every process has a stub before you rely on it being fast and harmless.

:::

::: {.callout-note}
A dry run passing means a plan could be built. A stub run passing means the graph is connected. Neither means the tool commands are right or that the results are correct. That still needs a tiny real input and a ground-truth check.
:::
